_note: The states of the Codex login (#68, #35) and what the board's free signals say about each. Every record says `observed` (true: seen on the box, codex-cli 0.161.0, 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-10) or false (not seen: written from the adapter's verdict rules and from Codex's source, never captured; a record built from the source says `from_source`). Nothing here comes from an auth.json: the board treats that file as opaque bytes. Logged in, logged out (no auth.json) and unreadable (empty or garbage auth.json) are observed for `codex login status`; `codex exec` was run in the same three logged-out states on 2026-10-10 and all three look the same (see `exec_no_login`). Only the server-rejected state (an expired or revoked login) was never seen: its texts are FROM SOURCE (openai/codex at commit 979011409de0a60b52f179721948e65531d26144, tag rust-v0.161.0, files under codex-rs/), recorded in `expired_revoked.from_source` with the file of each string; they are not observed, because producing them needs a real login that the server has revoked. A real dead login has to confirm them. An interactive session's rejected login is read from the pane (`expired_revoked.pane`, from source as well).

login_status.basis: Observed on the box, codex-cli 0.161.0, 2026-10-09: `codex login status` printed this line on stderr (not stdout) and exited 0. `login status` has no --json option (its --help lists only -c, --enable, --disable).

rollout.basis: A real token_count event of a working turn on 0.161.0 (box check 86). Only the outer timestamp is added here; the capture was the payload alone.

login_status.basis: Observed on the box, codex-cli 0.161.0, 2026-10-09 and again 2026-10-10, with a scratch CODEX_HOME holding no auth.json (no real account was logged out).

FROM SOURCE, not observed (openai/codex 979011409de0a60b52f179721948e65531d26144): `codex login status` (cli/src/login.rs run_login_status) only calls load_auth, which reads the saved login and never refreshes or asks the server, so a login the server rejects prints `Logged in using ChatGPT` on STDERR and exits 0, the same as a live one (stderr, like the observed logged_in case).

rollout.basis: SYNTHETIC SHAPE with the source's text. At 979011409de0a60b52f179721948e65531d26144 Codex does NOT write an error event to the rollout: rollout/src/policy.rs should_persist_event_msg lists EventMsg::Error under 'Transient, non-durable events' and returns false (the same arm in rust-v0.145.0 and rust-v0.160.0). So a login the server rejects most likely leaves nothing about the failure in the rollout, only a turn_complete. The board's rollout reader still accepts an event_msg error item (this file: message from manager.rs:208, codex_error_info `unauthorized` as protocol/src/error.rs sets it for RefreshTokenFailed), so it would work if a Codex version persisted it. Do not count on it.

exec.basis: FROM SOURCE, not observed. The TEXTS are the source's; the SEQUENCE (thread.started, turn.started, one error, turn.failed with the same message, nothing retried) is ASSUMED from the source: RefreshTokenFailed is in CodexErrorDetails::retry_delay's no-retry list (protocol/src/error.rs), exec turns an EventMsg::Error into an `error` event and a failed turn into turn.failed (exec/src/event_processor_with_jsonl_output.rs). Never captured; needs a genuinely dead login.

strings.name: REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRED_MESSAGE
strings.text: Your access token could not be refreshed because your refresh token has expired. Please log out and sign in again.
strings.when: the refresh endpoint answers error code refresh_token_expired

strings.name: REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED_MESSAGE
strings.text: Your access token could not be refreshed because your refresh token was already used. Please log out and sign in again.

strings.name: REFRESH_TOKEN_INVALIDATED_MESSAGE

strings.name: REFRESH_TOKEN_UNKNOWN_MESSAGE
strings.text: Your access token could not be refreshed. Please log out and sign in again.
strings.when: a 401 from the refresh endpoint, or a 400 invalid_grant, with any other code

strings.name: REFRESH_TOKEN_ACCOUNT_MISMATCH_MESSAGE
strings.text: Your access token could not be refreshed because you have since logged out or signed in to another account. Please sign in again.
strings.when: auth.json changed to another account while the process ran (what a board account switch does to an older process)
strings.verdict: NOT a dead login: the matcher leaves it out

strings.name: a 401 from the Responses API
strings.text: unexpected status 401 Unauthorized: <body>, url: <url>, cf-ray: <id>, request id: <id>, auth error: <header>, auth error code: token_expired
strings.when: the server answers 401 after the reload and refresh recovery steps (core/src/client.rs handle_unauthorized) were used up; the body is the error.message of a JSON body or the raw body, and `auth error code` is the x-error-json header's code (codex-api/src/api_bridge.rs)

strings.name: CLOUD_CONFIG_BUNDLE_AUTH_RECOVERY_FAILED_MESSAGE
strings.text: Your authentication session could not be refreshed automatically. Please log out and sign in again.
strings.when: the workspace-managed policies could not be loaded after a failed refresh

strings.name: the server's own wording for a reused refresh token
strings.text: Your refresh token has already been used to generate a new access token. Please try signing in again.
strings.when: only inside the refresh response body; Codex shows the constants above instead

strings.name: error kind
strings.when: codex_error_info of the error event for RefreshTokenFailed (other 401s carry http_connection_failed with status 401)

from_source.turn_failed_and_error_event: A failed refresh is CodexErr::RefreshTokenFailed (client.rs handle_unauthorized), displayed as its bare message, not prefixed with `unexpected status 401`. It is not retried.

pane.basis: FROM SOURCE, not observed. The Codex TUI draws an error event as one red history line `■ {message}` (codex-rs/tui/src/history_cell/notices.rs:331 new_error_event, called from chatwidget/turn_runtime.rs:372 on_error); an agent reply starts with `•` and the user's prompt with `›`. Because Codex 0.145 to 0.161 does not persist error events to the rollout (rollout/src/policy.rs:142), the pane is the only trace of a rejected login in an interactive session. The board (codex_pane.rejected_login, Tailer._pane_auth) raises login_problem for a `■ ` line, joined with up to three wrapped continuation lines, that matches the strict subset login_problem.CODEX_PANE_RE: 'access token could not be refreshed', 'authentication session could not be refreshed', 'auth error code: token_'. How a long message wraps across pane lines is ASSUMED, not captured.

exec_no_login.seconds: 25 to 30 (five retries on the websocket, five on https)
exec_no_login.stderr_repeats: failed to connect to websocket: HTTP error: 401 Unauthorized
exec_no_login.basis: Observed on the box, 2026-10-10: events thread.started, turn.started, four error 'Reconnecting... N/5 (unexpected status 401 Unauthorized: Missing bearer or basic authentication in header ...)', one item.completed of type error 'Falling back from WebSockets to HTTPS transport ...', five more error, a final error, then turn.failed with the 401 message. The fixture keeps that order and wording; request ids, cf-ray values and urls are replaced by <scrubbed>, and the text the recording elided ('...') is not invented. `exec` does not report a bad auth.json as a parse error, so only `codex login status` tells missing from unreadable.
